headline: Math benchmarks saturate while real-world agent work remains the bottleneck
outlook: Math is where progress has been fastest: 95% of the remaining headroom closed over the past year, FrontierMath crossed 90% in September, and GPT-6.1 Sol has just posted 100% on FrontierMath Tier 4. Agents and real work closed only 34% of their headroom, the slowest of any category. A September run of APEX-Agents records lifted the best score from 68.6% to 82.2%, but broader measures like the Remote Labor Index (20.8%) and OSWorld 2 (31.4%) suggest models are still far from reliably doing whole jobs, and Terminal-Bench and GeoBench have stalled short of 90% despite trends that said they should have arrived months ago. The underlying ingredients keep improving quickly: the longest task horizon is now 17.4 hours and doubling about every 4.1 months, which on current trends puts a full 40-hour work-week most likely around December 2026, though the plausible range runs to August 2027, while the cheapest model scoring 80% or better on GPQA has fallen from $3.44 to $0.055 per million tokens. Over the next year, the question is whether longer horizons and falling costs translate into the agent benchmarks that have lagged so far. These are extrapolations, and past likely ranges caught the real date only 59% of the time, typically missing by around five months.
